newsitem.title: INDIA: Indo-Rama, Itochu, Mitsui Petro plan JV.
newsitem.headline: Indo-Rama, Itochu, Mitsui Petro plan JV.

text.p: Indo-Rama Synthetics (India) Ltd has signed a memorandum of understanding to form a joint venture with two Japanese firms to build a purified terephthalic acid (PTA) plant, managing director O.P. Lohia said on Tuesday.

Indo Rama, the second largest producer of polyester in India, will retain a 60 percent stake in the joint venture, and the rest will be split between Japan's Itochu Corp and Mitsui Petrochemical Industries.
The project, being set up at Parwada near the port city of Visakhapatnam in the South Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, will cost 12 billion rupees ($336 million).
The equity component of the investment will be four billion rupees. Indo-Rama will contribute 2.4 billion rupees and the two Japanese collaborators will invest 1.6 billion rupees.

"The business viability of the project is assured as bulk of the production will be for captive consumption. Moreover, the low-cost production will ensure that we are highly competitive in the national and international markets," Lohia said.
The PTA project will be set up through a new company -- Indo-Rama Petrochemicals Limited -- to be registered and based in Andhra Pradesh.
Hara Sawa, director, Itochu Corporation, said the plant is the single largest foreign investment in Andhra Pradesh and the largest investment by a Japanese firm in India.
The PTA plant will have a capacity of 350,000 tonnes per annum (TPA) and is scheduled to be commissioned by the end of 1999. ($1.00 - 35.70)
